subject: Aurora onboarding: activation roadmap, integration milestones, and canary safeguards
messages:
From: Sophia Delgado <sophia.delgado@aurorabank.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Roe <tim.roe@aurorabank.com>; procurement@aurorabank.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP follow-up: implementation sequencing and safety gates

Marcus —

Thanks for the RFP response packet — procurement asked us to get a detailed activation roadmap and the canary/rollback criteria before the executive steering call next week. Specifically they want:

- Week-by-week milestone timeline for integration and go-live (including internal testing windows).
- Network and security requirements (VPC peering, NAT, KMS integration) and any items that require our infra changes.
- Canary schedule (percentages, metrics, duration) and automatic fallback conditions.
- Validation / acceptance criteria you expect from Aurora to confirm cutover.

Can you send a concise plan we can include in the procurement packet? We prefer concrete dates/windows and any critical dependencies.

Thanks,
Sophia Delgado
Senior Product Manager
Aurora Financial Services
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Delgado <sophia.delgado@aurorabank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: implementation sequencing and safety gates

Sophia —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a compact activation roadmap and our recommended canary/runbook artifacts (attached: redwood_activation_playbook_v1.pdf, aurora_canary_runbook.xlsx). Summary below — I focused on concrete windows and the minimal infra changes required on your side.

High-level schedule (target: mid-December pilot, full cutover late-Jan):
- Week 0 (Nov 15–21): Kickoff, credential exchange, compliance signoffs (KMS proof-of-possession), and shared runbook review.
- Week 1 (Nov 22–28): Network validation — VPC peering tests, NAT route confirmation, egress firewall rules. We provide a network_peering_checklist.txt for your infra team.
- Week 2–3 (Nov 29–Dec 12): Integration sandbox testing — API connectivity, sample workload runs, KV cache warmup patterns. Redwood provides test harness and 10k-token/day test credits.
- Week 4 (Dec 13–19): Canary pilot (region: us-east-1) — progressive traffic shift starting at 1% for 24h, 5% for 48h, 20% for 72h, decision point.
- Week 6 (Dec 27–Jan 2): Internal resilience testing & final rollback rehearsals (no customer traffic).
- Week 10 (Jan 24–30): Full production cutover window (low-traffic weekend), post-cutover 14-day observation.

Canary details (from aurora_canary_runbook.xlsx):
- Start: 1% of requests routed to Redwood for 24 hours. Acceptance metrics must be met over moving 1-hour windows: error_rate < 0.5%, p95 latency < 250ms, model-output QA pass >= 98% on a shared prompt set.
- Escalation: If any metric breaches for 2 consecutive windows, automatic rollback to incumbent model + pager to both teams.
- Progressive ramp: 1% → 5% (48h) → 20% (72h) → decision to continue or stop. Each ramp requires a signed ack from Aurora ops (can be Slack + email).

Dependencies (Aurora action items):
- Provide VPC peering CIDR allowlist and a reachable test endpoint by Nov 24.
- KMS access policy or signed attestation for key usage (we support bring-your-own-KMS) by Nov 21.
- Designated SRE contact and on-call window for canary days.

Acceptance / cutover criteria:
- All canary metrics met for 72h at 20% and no unresolved P1 incidents.
- Signed production readiness doc (we’ll prepare a short checklist) by Aurora engineering and LAURA (CS).

Attachments: redwood_activation_playbook_v1.pdf — covers runbook, roles & responsibilities, rollback play; aurora_canary_runbook.xlsx — ramp schedule and metrics; network_peering_checklist.txt — quick checklist for infra.

Next steps: we’ll schedule a 45-minute workshop Thursday to walk through the runbook and confirm dates. Laura will coordinate the invite. Happy to adjust the ramp cadence if you have heavier traffic patterns.

Best,
Marcus Lin
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: implementation sequencing and safety gates

Marcus / Laura —

Quick technical clarifications for the workshop:
1) API auth: We'll support mutual TLS or token-based auth. Recommendation: mTLS for the production canary; token for sandbox. Please confirm Aurora's preference so I can include exact curl examples.
2) KV cache pre-warm: For customers with heavy long-history prompts, we recommend a 48h pre-warm window with sample traces. We'll need a 10k-sample prompt set from Aurora (anonymized) or we can synthesize if policy disallows sharing.
3) Monitoring: We'll provide a Grafana dashboard (read-only link) and push alert definitions into your PagerDuty. We need the PD service id by Dec 4.

I'll be on the Thu workshop to run the network validation checklist. Attached the minimal network ports we need in the checklist (network_peering_checklist.txt).

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Tim Roe <tim.roe@aurorabank.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophia Delgado <sophia.delgado@aurorabank.com>; karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>; laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: implementation sequencing and safety gates

Marcus / Karthik —

This looks reasonable. A couple of clarifications from engineering:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood requires public egress for token refresh calls, or can those be routed via our internal NAT with no public IP?
- For KMS, we need a short integration doc (API calls, envelopes) to circulate to our security team. If you have a one-page summary that would be ideal.

Also: procurement asked whether Redwood supports a staged data retention policy (30/90/365 day tiers) at the API layer. We will not store customer content beyond agreed retention, but we need the service to support a per-tenant retention TTL. Is that available out-of-the-box or is it a configuration change?

Thanks — I’ll bring these to the workshop unless you want to send answers now.

—Tim
VP Engineering, Aurora Financial Services
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tim Roe <tim.roe@aurorabank.com>, Sophia Delgado <sophia.delgado@aurorabank.com>, procurement@aurorabank.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: implementation sequencing and safety gates

Tim —

Answers inline and a short note on retention:

- Egress: Redwood supports routing token refresh and telemetry via your internal NAT; no public IP required. We will need outbound connectivity to our identity endpoint over TLS (443) but this can flow through your NAT — we’ll validate during the network test.

- KMS one-pager: attached in the activation playbook and I’ll pull the KMS summary into the workshop slides. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations. The flow is envelope encryption with customer-managed keys.

- Retention: Redwood supports per-tenant retention policies in the control plane. Default retention tiers (30 / 90 / 365) are configurable per tenant; we can lock retention at provisioning time and provide audit logs for deletions. We’ll include the configuration snippet in the playbook and add it to the Postman collection for sandbox testing.

Next: Laura will circulate the calendar invite for Thu 11/13 10:00–10:45 PT workshop. I’ll bring the runbook and KMS one-pager; Karthik will run network tests. Please review the attachments ahead of the workshop.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_activation_playbook_v1.pdf, aurora_canary_runbook.xlsx, network_peering_checklist.txt
